Direction_Note: Negative: larger separation → weaker flux linkage → lower M
Physical_Context: Wire-to-wire centre distance. Larger separation reduces mutual inductive coupling (decreasing M) and reduces inter-wire capacitance (decreasing C). Dominant control parameter for both EMC properties.

Direction_Note: Negative: shorter pitch → better cancellation → lower effective M
Physical_Context: Twist pitch of the pair. Shorter pitch improves field cancellation, reducing effective mutual inductance. Has moderate effect on capacitance through wire spacing geometry.

Direction_Note: Positive: longer overlap → more coupled length → higher M
Physical_Context: Length of parallel run between pairs. Mutual inductance scales nearly linearly with overlap (more parallel conductor = more flux linkage). No significant effect on per-metre capacitance (hence excluded from cap model).
